root: ^MARÍA: "In Republika, in the City of Man-- lie bodies.
^Don’t worry, I tell you this not to scare you.
^I speak from a place of inevitability and pity.
^You seem to be holding your breath. I wonder how long you sensed me hovering, darkening every corner. I muse too if you can hear the cries of your neighbour over the drone of turning gears."
^1. I try to. It is tiring.

c-0: ^ YOU: "I try to. It is tiring."
^María smiles knowingly. You think it looks kind.
g-0: ^MARÍA: "Then relax, and let me tell you the odds.

^There is a rot in the heart of the Republika-- and you are just a man. With your own life and needs to worry about. Your soul cannot remain whole if it is consumed by the needs of the body. Does the ache feel familiar to you yet?
^I think the symphony was only meant for the next world anyways- for better people. It is far too late for us here."

c-1: ^1. The prayer you mutter comes easily.
^María waits and listens, but a glance tells you she is not moved.

g-1: ^MARÍA:  "Hmm. Such is life, eh? Maybe you’ll be born luckier next time.
^Bahala na. Matulog na tayo. Let the drone become a lullaby."

c-2: ^It is easy to rest and forget the world.

g-2: ^MARÍA: "It’s so still here, I could almost hear your soul sigh—soft, resigned.  Perhaps it is content. Or… perhaps it is weary. The line between the two is thin, too thin to be certain.

c-4: ^Simply resting is doing well for you. A true distraction would be excessive.

Accept: ^You don't see it, but somewhere in the back of your mind, a radio knob is turned. Its sound crackles to life, spilling out a mess of tones that rise but never truly peak.
^María's feet shuffle and pad around to what should be a beat. Even past when the radio picks up static.
Radio_News: ^The radio drops to a new frequency. Out splutters the voice of someone reading on the other end.
^RADIO: "In a scattered archipelago-- (...) ...I'd be happy to slaug-- (...) ...a whore! I will curse-- (...)"

s: ^1. Attempt to turn the radio off.

Reject: ^Aha! Don’t tell me– you see yourself brave, only to end up standing in-front of a firing squad. Or maybe you’d prefer to be comfortable at the end and choose the slow boil. Either way–
^Why resist, if the world will continue to spin crooked without you anyway?"

c-0: ^ YOU: "Well, what happens when we run out of tinder to burn?"
